extracted.intended_audience: physicists, scientists, and students/readers of philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to form and evaluate conceptual/mechanical models in physical science (particles, ether, laws of motion), emphasizing what assumptions and idealizations are legitimate and how to test their applicability by reference to perceptual experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science's proper aim: description not metaphysical explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: "the object of science, which is not to explain but to describe by conceptual shorthand our perceptual experience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not project conceptual symbols (geometrical ideals, mechanism) into the phenomenal world as if they were realities; science should focus on describing changes of sense-impression and using conceptual models as shorthand for prediction rather than asserting ultimate metaphysical causes. Anti-pattern: treating concepts like motion, matter, or force as literal realities to be explained rather than useful descriptive tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for introducing idealized entities (e.g., particles)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is the particle a symbol by aid of which we can describe our past and predict our future sequences of sense-impressions with a great and uniform degree of accuracy? If it be, then its use is justified as a scientific method of simplifying our ideas and economizing thought."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce idealizations (particles, corpuscles) only when they demonstrably enable concise, accurate description and prediction of perceptual routines. Example: Newton's particles justify his law of gravitation by the law's empirical power. Scoring note: prefer models that economize thought while maintaining empirical adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for assumptions: necessity for descriptive economy
rubrics_metrics.description: "The test will always be the same, namely: How far is the assumption necessary in order to obtain a model which will enable us to describe briefly the routine of perception?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate hypotheses and added assumptions by whether they are necessary to produce a model that succinctly describes and predicts perceptual experience. Avoid superfluous structure that does not improve descriptive or predictive power. Use experimental verification on perceptual equivalents (observable bodies) as the deciding test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit extension of mechanical laws across scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Modes of motion peculiar to gross 'matter' must arise from its special structure, and ... they cannot be extended to the ether in general. ... Ought we to assert that these laws hold in their entirety for all the scale from particle to ether-element? ... The question ... cannot be answered offhand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not uncritically extend laws derived for one level (particles, molecules) to more fundamental levels (prime-atoms, ether-elements) without justification. Consider structural differences and test whether extending a law simplifies description or introduces unsupported complexity. Anti-pattern: assuming Newtonian laws apply unchanged at every conceptual scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: First general law of motion for corpuscles (modeling principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every corpuscle in the conceptual model of the universe must be conceived as moving with due regard to the presence of every other corpuscle, although for very distant corpuscles the regard paid is extremely small as compared with that paid to immediate neighbours."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In models, account for mutual influence among all corpuscles, with influence diminishing with distance. Use this as a baseline modeling principle when constructing dynamical descriptions of bodies. Practical guidance: neglect influences that are negligibly small for the phenomena of interest (see idealization rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediated interaction formulation (ether mediation alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every corpuscle, whether of ether or gross 'matter' influences the motion of the adjacent ether corpuscles, and through them of every other corpuscle, however distant; the influence thus spread is nevertheless very insignificant at great as compared with small distances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modeling action-at-a-distance phenomena, consider formulations where interactions are mediated through adjacent elements (e.g., ether-elements) rather than assumed to be direct across arbitrary distances. This provides an alternative interpretive rubric and avoids naive metaphysical assumptions about direct distant action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of idealization: neglect influences beyond measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: "we neglect at once influences which even in the aggregate are beyond our powers of measurement. Further, we purposely exclude from consideration slight, if measurable, variations of motion due to more distant groups. We isolate a particular group of corpuscles..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify models by excluding influences that lie below measurement thresholds or are irrelevant to predictive aims. Isolate and analyze subsystems when appropriate. Scoring note: legitimate simplifications are those that do not materially reduce empirical accuracy for the intended descriptions/predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid metaphysical causal attributions for 'why' questions
rubrics_metrics.description: On asking 'Why do bodies move?' the text emphasizes: 'When we...phenomenalize the ether... we still are left with the problem: Why does ether-matter move? ... We don't know.' and suggests it is better to 'cease supposing that any lucid explanation of the why of motion can be abstracted from the idea of force.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject or bracket metaphysical explanations (e.g., attributing motion to will or hidden 'force' as ultimate cause) when they do not correspond to observable sense-impressions. Prefer descriptive laws that capture regularities rather than asserting ultimate causes. Anti-pattern: substituting names ('force', 'will') for explanatory content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware infinite regress in mechanistic explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: "To appeal to the conception of elasticity is only to 'explain' one 'action at a distance' by a second 'action at a distance.' If the ether-elements owe their elasticity to such an arrangement, we shall want another ether to 'explain' the motion of the first, and the process will have to be continued ad infinitum."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid constructing explanations that merely push the explanatory burden to a deeper, similarly problematic layer ad infinitum. If a proposed mechanism requires an endless chain of further mechanisms, treat the construction with suspicion and consider adopting descriptive or pragmatic accounts instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of empirical power and economy for accepting laws
rubrics_metrics.description: "The justification of the law of gravitation lies in the power it gives us of constructing the motion of the groups of particles by aid of which we symbolize physical bodies and ultimately describe and predict the routine of our sense-impressions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept laws primarily for their empirical efficacy: their capacity to enable construction of models that accurately describe and predict observable phenomena, while economizing thought. Prefer theories that combine simplicity (economy) with wide descriptive/predictive reach.
